user.title: PalPulse for Home Assistant
user.description: Enter the Powerpal BLE MAC address. The ESPHome node must emit PalPulse timestamped record events.

error.invalid_mac: Enter a valid six-byte MAC address (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF).

abort.already_configured: This Powerpal meter is already configured.

flat.title: Flat electricity tariff
flat.description: Enter your actual electricity rate and optional daily supply fee in cents. Confirm rates against your bill.

time_of_use.title: Time of use / free power
time_of_use.description: Enter your actual peak, shoulder, off-peak and optional free electricity windows. Times follow Home Assistant's local timezone. For Red Power5, verify your free hours and daily allowance against your bill.

data_description.daily_free_cap_kwh: For Red Power5, enter 15; for Red Midday Power Saver, 24
data_description.free_excess_cents_per_kwh: Red Power5 previously used 16.412 c/kWh in your local configuration. Verify current bill before use.

pricing.title: Electricity pricing
pricing.description: Choose Home Assistant's pricing (default), an Australian flat rate, or a custom time-of-use tariff. PalPulse external energy statistics require their own cost statistic for Energy dashboard cost tracking.

historical_costs.title: Previous cost history
historical_costs.description: Choose how your old electricity costs were recorded. Next you'll select the actual source from a visual Home Assistant picker. A cost-per-kWh price sensor is not historical cost data.

data_description.legacy_cost_source_mode: Select your prior data format. The next screen offers a visual picker.

cost_source_statistic.title: Select an existing cumulative cost statistic
cost_source_statistic.description: Choose a recorded lifetime monetary total with cumulative hourly sums. A price-per-kWh sensor is not a historical cost. Leave empty to clear the previous source.

cost_source_daily.title: Select your previous daily electricity cost sensor
cost_source_daily.description: Choose a sensor whose **recorded hourly closing states** hold the running total cost since local midnight. For example, a verified daily-reset electricity cost entity. Missing or ambiguous days are skipped. Leave empty to clear the source.

energy_history.title: Electricity usage history
energy_history.description: Review and manage the earlier Powerpal kWh import. You cannot import without a successful Preview and a fresh verified backup.

cost_history.title: Historical electricity costs

energy_preview.title: Preview Powerpal usage history

cost_preview.title: Preview historical electricity costs

energy_import.title: Confirm Powerpal history import
energy_import.description: **This changes PalPulse's historical energy statistic.** The original source `{source}` and existing readings at and after cutover remain untouched. Home Assistant must create and verify a Recorder-inclusive backup before any write. The preview covers {rows} rows. **Only continue if you reviewed it.**

data.confirm_action: I reviewed the preview and authorise a backed-up import

cost_import.title: Confirm historical cost import
cost_import.description: **This changes PalPulse's historical cost statistic only.** The original cost source `{source}` is never changed. A fresh Recorder-inclusive backup is required, and existing live cost rows are preserved. The preview covers {rows} rows.

data.confirm_action: I reviewed the cost preview and authorise a backed-up import

energy_resume.title: Resume the interrupted usage import
energy_resume.description: PalPulse will verify the original backup and every already-written historical row before continuing. Conflicting data stops the operation. The old source is unchanged.

data.confirm_action: Resume and reconcile the interrupted usage import

cost_resume.title: Resume the interrupted cost import
cost_resume.description: PalPulse will verify the original backup and existing historical cost rows before continuing. It will not overwrite unmatched data.

data.confirm_action: Resume and reconcile the interrupted cost import

energy_undo.title: Undo imported usage history
energy_undo.description: **Destructive operation for imported PalPulse history only.** PalPulse creates and verifies a fresh Recorder-inclusive backup and removes only journalled historical rows before the original cutover. Original Powerpal usage and live PalPulse hours are preserved.

data.confirm_action: I understand and authorise removing the imported usage history

cost_undo.title: Undo imported historical costs
cost_undo.description: **Destructive operation for imported cost history only.** A fresh Recorder-inclusive backup is created first. Only journalled, verified imported cost rows are removed. Original costs and energy history are preserved.

data.confirm_action: I understand and authorise removing the imported costs

overview.title: PalPulse status overview

free_hours.title: Free electricity hours
free_hours.description: Use these time pickers when the **same free-power window applies every day**. For the older Red Energy Red Power5 offer, the commonly configured window is 11:00 am to 4:00 pm with up to 15 kWh free daily. Confirm your actual plan and rate on your bill. This screen preserves your existing peak and shoulder schedules. To configure different weekday/weekend free windows, use the advanced Time of Use pricing screen.

data_description.daily_free_cap_kwh: Enter 0 only if your offer provides unlimited free usage in this window.
data_description.free_excess_cents_per_kwh: Enter the rate in cents per kWh specified by your retailer for usage after the free allowance. Verify the bill; no rate is assumed.

wizard.title: PalPulse guided setup
wizard.description: Choose what to configure. Each screen explains the setting, and you review everything before it is saved. **No old energy or cost history is imported by this wizard.** Red Power5 is a convenience preset, not proof of your retailer's current terms.

data.setup_goal: Choose your electricity plan or setup task

wizard_red_power5.title: Red Energy Power5: confirm actual prices
wizard_red_power5.description: The suggested free-power hours are **11:00–16:00 daily** with **15 kWh/day free**. Check that these match your actual Red Energy bill. **Enter all paid rates from your bill.** No paid-rate value has been assumed. This screen keeps existing peak/shoulder schedules, which you can adjust under Electricity pricing.

wizard_cost_choice.title: Do you want to connect old electricity cost history?
wizard_cost_choice.description: This step is optional. Connecting a previously recorded cost source **does not import anything**. You can return later through Historical electricity costs. Existing energy history and tariffs remain unchanged.

data.configure_old_costs: Select an existing historical cost source now

wizard_cost_type.title: How was your old electricity cost recorded?
wizard_cost_type.description: A **cumulative** statistic keeps an ever-increasing total. A **daily-reset** sensor starts a new daily total at midnight. Select the appropriate type. Current-price-per-kWh sensors are not historical costs.

wizard_cost_picker.title: Choose your previous electricity cost source
wizard_cost_picker.description: Select the actual recorded source from Home Assistant. This step only configures the ID. PalPulse later validates the historical data in a read-only Preview, and will block unsafe imports.

wizard_review.title: Review your PalPulse configuration

dashboard.title: Create your PalPulse Control Centre dashboard
dashboard.description:
The dashboard uses **built-in Home Assistant cards**, so no extra HACS frontend component is needed.

1. In Home Assistant, open **Settings > Dashboards > Add dashboard > New dashboard from scratch**. Name it *PalPulse Control Centre*.
2. Open the new dashboard, choose **Edit > Raw configuration editor**.
3. Copy the [PalPulse dashboard template](https://github.com/iamhasantan/palpulse-homeassistant/blob/main/dashboards/palpulse-control-centre.yaml) into the editor.
4. Replace each `YOURMAC` in the template with **{meter}**. Verify the sensor entity IDs under **PalPulse > Entities**, since they may differ by installation.
5. Save. The dashboard shows energy and cost graphs plus migration progress, and does **not** include dangerous Import or Undo controls.

**Energy statistic:** `{energy_statistic}`

**Cost statistic:** `{cost_statistic}`

This step will not create or overwrite any existing dashboard. It is an optional one-time manual import to avoid relying on unstable Home Assistant dashboard-management internals.

error.invalid_pricing: Invalid rate, free allowance or tariff window. Check for overlapping peak/shoulder periods.
error.invalid_source: Choose a valid historical cost sensor or statistic other than PalPulse's target cost statistic.
error.migration_locked: Undo the previous cost migration before changing its source or source type. Existing history was left untouched.
error.confirmation_required: Tick the confirmation checkbox before any data is changed.
error.source_required: Select a recorded historical electricity cost source, or return to the previous step and skip this part.

abort.history_unavailable: Migration tools are not loaded. Check PalPulse integration status and try again.
abort.history_busy: A migration is already running. Review the migration status before starting another.
abort.history_already_started: A previous import already exists. Use Resume for interrupted work or Undo for a completed import.
abort.nothing_to_resume: There is no interrupted import that can be resumed.
abort.nothing_to_undo: There is no recorded historical import to undo.
abort.preview_complete: The read-only preview has finished. No data was imported.
abort.enable_tou_first: Choose a custom time-of-use electricity tariff first. Then return to this screen to configure free electricity with time pickers.
abort.overview_complete: Status overview closed. No configuration was changed.
abort.wizard_unavailable: This setup step is unavailable. Restart the PalPulse Configure wizard.
abort.dashboard_guide_complete: Dashboard instructions closed. No Home Assistant dashboard or settings were changed.

progress.processing_history: Backing up, processing and verifying {operation}. You can also monitor the PalPulse migration status and progress sensors.
